review_candidates.title: Transport Network - Support Manager (PMO) Thailand
review_candidates.description: Job description: The position reports to the Head, Transport Network Job Overview: We are looking for a results-driven Support Manager (PMO) based in Thailand to serve as the on-the-ground extension of TIME's Transport Network organisation in ASEAN. This hybrid role combines project delivery, regional network operations, and subsea investment co-management: you will support the design, rollout and operation of ASEAN cross-country terrestrial connectivity, while co-managing TIME's portfolio of submarine cable investments to maximise technical, operational and financial value. You'll act as the key link between TIME HQ (Kuala Lumpur) and Thailand operations, ensuring projects and subsea assets are delivered, maintained and commercially optimised in line with HQ strategy. Your work life: ASEAN Terrestrial Connectivity — Project Delivery & Planning Lead end-to-end planning and execution of ASEAN cross-country terrestrial network programs (backbone builds, DWDM expansion, data-centre interconnection routes) originating from or transiting Thailand. Develop master schedules using MS Project and manage dependencies, risks, budgets, and stakeholder communication across multi-country teams. Align design and rollout timelines with HQ teams (OSP, Subsea, Optical Engineering) to ensure Thailand-based projects integrate cleanly into the wider ASEAN network topology. Support proposals for new or upgraded terrestrial and ASEAN connectivity routes, providing local market and regulatory input for HQ's investment considerations. Work closely with Finance and Planning teams to develop budgets, forecasts, and long-range investment plans for Thailand and cross-border connectivity initiatives. Subsea Portfolio Co-Management Co-manage TIME's portfolio of submarine cable investments (consortium and private cable systems) landing in or transiting Thailand, to maximise benefit from a technical, operational and financial perspective. Support HQ in tracking cable system performance, capacity utilisation, and O&M cost efficiency, and in preparing business cases for capacity upgrades, IRU sales/purchases, or additional investments. Represent TIME in local consortium, landing party, and cable maintenance agreement (CMA) matters, coordinating with HQ on consortium meetings, votes, and strategic decisions. Liaise with cable landing stations, marine maintenance providers, and local authorities to ensure landing point operations, permits, and repair readiness are maintained to consortium standards. Monitor subsea system health, restoration plans, and route diversity, escalating risks to HQ and supporting mitigation and investment planning. Regional Network Operations Support backbone and PoP operations (fiber, DWDM, interconnects) supporting ASEAN connectivity in Thailand. Coordinate permits, site access, and preventive maintenance with local partners and vendors. Ensure SLA compliance across terrestrial and subsea-dependent services, and provide weekly operational reports to HQ. Technical Support (TAC Interface) Support Tier-3 escalations for DWDM, ROADM, and subsea systems, coordinating with vendors and HQ engineering teams to restore service and prevent recurrence. Efficiently and effectively support the operation and maintenance of all subsea systems within scope, sustaining their competitiveness and strategic importance to the Company. Regulatory & Compliance Support HQ in liaising with Thai telecom authorities (NBTC) to ensure legal and regulatory compliance for terrestrial and cable landing operations. Support licensing, permits, and cross-border connectivity approvals for ASEAN network projects. Maintain documentation for audits, consortium reporting, and regulatory submissions. To be considered, you’ll need: Bachelor's Degree in Telecommunications, Electrical, or Network Engineering. 7–10 years of experience in transport network, OSP operations, or project delivery, including cross-border/ASEAN network exposure. 8+ years of experience in Subsea or international network operations, including submarine cable construction, consortium activities, and cable maintenance agreements. Direct experience co-managing or supporting submarine cable investment portfolios — capacity planning, O&M cost management, and business case development. Fluent in Thai & English; strong knowledge of local regulatory and cable landing requirements. Expertise in DWDM / Optical Transport Systems (Ciena, Infinera, Huawei) and their integration with subsea line terminal equipment. Skilled in MS Project, Smartsheet, Primavera; strong vendor and consortium management experience. Excellent leadership, coordination, and cross-functional communication skills across HQ and regional stakeholders. Our Commitment to You At Time, we believe great work deserves great support. Here’s what you can look forward to when you join us: Comprehensive medical coverage for you and your immediate family, including outpatient care, hospitalisation, dental and optical benefits. Wellness support with an annual spending account for health-related needs, alternative treatments, or even paid-up premiums for personal insurance. Employee assistance during life’s big moments, from celebrations to times of bereavement. Learning & growth opportunities through dedicated time for learning, access to LinkedIn Learning and rewards for upskilling Cash rewards for recognised certifications and full reimbursement for up to two approved professional memberships each year

review_candidates.title: Staff Dimensional Engineer – SPARC
review_candidates.description: Devens, MA Corporate Operations – Quality / Full-time / On-site apply for this job About Commonwealth Fusion Systems Commonwealth Fusion Systems is on a mission to deliver the urgent transition to fusion energy. Combining decades of research, top talent, and new technologies, we’re designing and building commercially viable fusion power plants. And we're working with policymakers, suppliers, and many others to build the energy industry of the future. We’re in the best position to make it happen. Since 2018, we’ve raised $4 billion of capital, making us the largest and leading fusion company in the world. Now we’re looking for more thinkers, doers, builders, and makers to join us. People who’ll bring new perspectives, solve tough problems, and thrive as part of a team. If that’s you and this role fits, we want to hear from you. Join the power movement as a Staff Dimensional Engineer – SPARC SPARC is a first-of-a-kind machine, and it presents some of the hardest dimensional management problems in industry today: large high-field magnets, tight tolerances on complex geometries at meter scale, novel materials, and assembly stack-ups with no precedent to copy from. CFS is seeking a Staff Dimensional Engineer to be the technical authority for dimensional management across HTS Magnet production and the SPARC project. This is a role for someone who wants to define a discipline, not inherit one. You will own how design intent becomes buildable, verifiable hardware: setting GD&T and datum strategy with Engineering, analyzing variation propagation through assembly sequences before hardware proves it the hard way, and defining what we measure and to what acceptance criteria. Your decisions will shape how fusion hardware is toleranced, measured, and accepted, on SPARC and on the ARC power plants that follow. You will work alongside a metrology team equipped with laser trackers, portable CMM arms, and structured-light scanning, and with an established Quality Engineering organization that owns statistical process control and measurement system analysis, so your focus stays on the geometry. Learn how to create new-from-scratch SDSs as well as duplicate/translated SDSs for existing formulations. Screen safety documents (e.g., supplier SDSs) for chemical components involved. Support review and adjustment of existing SDSs as formulations, classifications, or regulations change. Assist with production and departmental review of label templates (GHS/CLP), under supervision. Archive all data related to each SDS request and release, including present master documents, following the department's document-retention rules. Provide frequent, specific status reporting on SDS/label workload to the Lead Manager. Responsibilities (Tasks) - introduced progressively, once SDS fundamentals are mastered: Cross-check the other Assistant's SDS/label releases before publication (mutual back-up model), and have releases cross-checked in return. Take on a rotating share of non-SDS regulatory-compliance support tasks alongside the second Assistant. Support PCN dossier creation and updates (new dossiers and amendments to existing ones). Support GHS/CLP labelling management, including keeping label templates current per product and per country. Support regulatory-change monitoring: periodic follow-up on worldwide regulatory updates via ExESS, reporting relevant changes to the Lead Manager. Support UFI number management. Provide logistics support for external laboratory analyses (scheduling, sample tracking, documentation). Support existing notification follow-up (e.g., US-EPA, EU-REACH, KR-REACH, UK-REACH, KKDIK) as capacity allows, under guidance. Support EU compliance requirements for non-EU production sites, once trained. Escalate genuinely critical or high-hazard (O/T/F) cases to the Lead Manager via the department's Think Tank process, rather than deciding independently. Required Qualifications: Proficient in English (written and spoken) is a must. Strong attention to detail and a structured, methodical way of working, critical for compliancesensitive documentation. Good communication and analytical skills; comfortable asking questions and working closely with a supervising RAA/Lead Manager while learning. Able to follow procedures precisely and to respect deadlines, including while still building expertise. MS Office proficient; willingness and aptitude to learn dedicated regulatory/SDS software (e.g., ExESS) and, in time, portals such as ECHA REACH-IT. Minimum of a bachelor’s degree (or equivalent), ideally in a scientific, chemical, EHS, or regulatory-related field. Genuine interest in regulatory affairs, product safety, or EHS as a career path. Required Experience: No prior SDS or regulatory-affairs experience is required, this is a developing role and full training is provided. Any prior exposure to the chemical industry, EHS, laboratory work, or regulatory/compliance environments is an asset but not mandatory. Permissions (only after 2Y and a positive evaluation): During the initial training period, all SDS releases, label releases, and regulatory submissions require review and sign-off by the Lead Manager or an authorized, more senior RAA. No independent release authority is granted from day one. What we offer: An attractive position in a global and dynamic company; This is full time remote positon; Opportunity for professional and personal development; Competitive employment conditions. Predictable & Consistent Work Schedule. Work on exciting projects that push the boundaries of what’s possible. Side notes: CV in English is required; Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

review_candidates.title: Project Manager
review_candidates.description: The Work Package Manager (Project Manager) is responsible for the overall leadership, management, and successful delivery of two offshore packages on a major offshore oil and gas facility in North Africa. The role, which will be performed from Milan , ensures the safe, timely, and cost-effective execution of engineering, procurement, fabrication, construction, transportation, offshore installation, pre-commissioning, commissioning support, and handover activities associated with the facilities and related platform modifications. The position serves as the primary focal point for all package activities, coordinating multidisciplinary teams, contractors, fabrication yards, certification bodies, marine contractors, and client stakeholders to ensure alignment with project objectives, contractual requirements, and operational readiness targets. The role is primarily based in Milan and requires regular travel to fabrication yards, contractor offices, ports, and offshore execution locations as required. Key Responsibilities Project Management & Leadership Lead and manage the Work Package in accordance with the approved Project Execution Plan (PEP). Establish execution priorities and ensure alignment between engineering, procurement, fabrication, transportation, installation, commissioning, and handover activities. Develop and maintain the execution strategy, objectives, milestones, and performance metrics. Provide leadership to multidisciplinary project teams and ensure effective collaboration across all project functions. Ensure compliance with HSE, quality, environmental, regulatory, and contractual requirements throughout project execution. Act as the primary focal point between the Client, Consortium, contractors, and project management team regarding package related matters. Engineering Management Oversee all engineering activities related to the jacket, topsides, living quarters, utilities, process systems, marine systems, and FMWR interfaces. Ensure timely review and approval of engineering deliverables, design changes, technical queries, and vendor documentation. Monitor engineering progress and address bottlenecks affecting procurement and construction activities. Coordinate constructability reviews, HAZOP/HAZID actions, model reviews, and design verification activities. Ensure effective management of technical interfaces between package modifications, subsea systems, drilling packages, and offshore operations. Procurement & Supply Chain Management Monitor procurement activities for critical equipment, long-lead items, bulk materials, and vendor packages. Ensure alignment between procurement schedules, fabrication requirements, and project milestones. Oversee expediting, inspection, logistics, and transportation activities. Support the resolution of supplier performance issues and delivery risks. Ensure procurement activities comply with contractual and project requirements. Construction & Fabrication Management Direct fabrication and construction activities across multiple fabrication yards and contractor facilities. Monitor productivity, progress, quality performance, and contractor resource deployment. Ensure construction activities are executed safely and in accordance with approved procedures and specifications. Lead resolution of fabrication issues, NCRs, construction constraints, and field engineering matters. Verify readiness for mechanical completion and handover activities. Installation & Marine Operations Oversee transportation, load-out, sea fastening, marine spread readiness, and offshore installation activities. Coordinate with transportation and installation contractors, marine warranty surveyors, certification authorities, and offshore stakeholders. Ensure offshore installation plans, procedures, risk assessments, and execution schedules are adequately reviewed and approved. Monitor offshore campaign readiness and ensure all prerequisites are achieved prior to execution. Lead resolution of marine and installation-related interfaces and risks. Contract & Commercial Management Administer WHPA package contractual obligations and ensure compliance by all parties. Review contractor performance against schedule, cost, quality, and contractual commitments. Evaluate and recommend approval of change orders, variation requests, claims, and progress payment applications. Support project controls in forecasting final cost, contingency requirements, and performance reporting. Participate in commercial negotiations and dispute resolution as required. Project Controls, Planning & Reporting Ensure development and maintenance of detailed schedules, recovery plans, and execution forecasts. Monitor progress against approved baselines and key project milestones. Identify schedule risks and implement mitigation and acceleration measures where required. Review cost reports, earned value metrics, and productivity indicators. Prepare regular reports and presentations for senior management and client stakeholders. Interface & Stakeholder Management Manage interfaces with Directorate, Onshore, Sealines, Subsea Modification, Drilling, Operations, and Commissioning teams. Coordinate activities among engineering contractors, fabrication yards, equipment vendors, certifying bodies, and operational stakeholders. Lead management meetings, progress reviews, and interface workshops. Ensure effective communication and alignment of project objectives across all stakeholders. Risk, Quality & HSE Management Promote a strong safety culture and ensure full compliance with project HSE requirements. Identify, assess, and manage technical, commercial, schedule, and operational risks. Ensure implementation of mitigation actions and contingency plans. Support audits, inspections, quality reviews, and certification activities. Ensure timely closure of non-conformances, punch list items, and corrective actions. Commissioning & Handover Support development of commissioning, start-up, and operational readiness strategies. Ensure completion and handover dossiers are prepared in accordance with project requirements. Coordinate mechanical completion, commissioning support, and final acceptance activities. Ensure Project close-out activities are completed efficiently and lessons learned are captured. Qualifications & Experience Bachelor's Degree in Mechanical, Civil, Structural, Marine, Offshore, Electrical, or related Engineering discipline. Professional Project Management qualification (PMP, IPMA, PRINCE2, or equivalent) preferred. Minimum 15 years of experience in the oil and gas industry. Minimum 10 years of experience managing major offshore EPC/EPCI/EPIC projects. Demonstrated experience with fixed offshore platforms, jackets, topsides, drilling facilities, and offshore installation campaigns. Experience managing multi-location fabrication and construction programs. Strong knowledge of offshore transportation and installation methodologies. Experience coordinating marine operations, certification activities, and marine warranty requirements. Excellent understanding of project controls, contract management, procurement, risk management, and project execution methodologies. Familiarity with international offshore codes and standards including API, ISO, IEC, DNV, SOLAS, and IMO requirements. Previous experience in Mediterranean, North African, or Middle East offshore oil and gas projects is highly desirable. Key Competencies Leadership and Team Management Offshore Project Execution EPCI/EPIC Project Management Strategic Planning and Decision Making Contract and Commercial Management Marine and Installation Operations Stakeholder and Interface Management Risk and Change Management Negotiation and Conflict Resolution HSE Leadership Quality Management Communication and Reporting
